note: Rugby league's built-in earlier seasons (docs/design/rugby-league.md, "Earlier seasons"): the 2008 NRL season from Rugby League 2: World Cup Edition's own database, every player checked against the Rugby League Project's 2008 records. node scripts/sync-rugby-league-seasons.mjs writes scripts/data/rugby-league-seasons/<id>.json from the inputs pinned in scripts/data/rugby-league-seasons-sources.json; node scripts/build-rugby-league-seasons.mjs builds each season's clubs; node scripts/build-club-maps.mjs --league=nrl builds each era's map from `teams` and `maps`. `teams` lists every club of a season by the database's name for it (`list`) and the Rugby League Project's (`rlp`, its first-grade season page, whose slug the season before shares, read only to say why a player is left out; `nyc`, its National Youth Competition one): `franchise` is today's club, `id` the season's own where the club has been renamed or moved since, `ground` where it played its home games (a ground it still plays at under its present name), `base` where a club that shared its ground trained, and `home` the [lon, lat] its territory grows from (English Wikipedia's coordinates). `nations` are the season's World Cup nations, by the database's name, the game's nation id, RLP's World Cup squad heading and its Test team code: the sync checks their squads, but the season fields clubs only (docs/design/rugby-league.md, "Earlier seasons"); `carriedOver` the database's national squads that are older editions' and are not read; `nameFixes` a name the database spells with a character no name has.

seasons.label: Rugby League 2: World Cup Edition
seasons.edition: Rugby League 2: World Cup Edition (PlayStation 2, Sidhe, 2008)
seasons.compiler: the game's own database (RLDatabase.xml), extracted from its data pak by Wouldubeinta and posted on rugbyleaguemods.net (thread "Data pak File", post 570, 30 March 2012, attachment 56); every player checked against the Rugby League Project's 2008 records; the overall is ours

2008.name: Bulldogs
2008.era: The club played as the Bulldogs from 2000 to 2009, Canterbury-Bankstown again from 2010; it shared its ground with the Rabbitohs and moved its training and offices from Belmore Sports Ground to Sydney Olympic Park, beside the ground, early in 2008 (English Wikipedia, Belmore Sports Ground).

2008.name: Melbourne Storm
2008.era: The Storm played at Olympic Park Stadium until AAMI Park opened in 2010; the stadium was demolished in 2012.

2008.name: North Queensland Cowboys
2008.era: The Cowboys played at the Willows Sports Complex in Kirwan, then Dairy Farmers Stadium, until the North Queensland Stadium opened in 2020.

2008.name: Parramatta Eels
2008.era: Parramatta Stadium was demolished in 2016; Western Sydney Stadium stands on its site.

2008.name: South Sydney Rabbitohs
2008.era: The Rabbitohs shared their ground with the Bulldogs. Redfern Oval was the club's training ground from 1988 until it moved to the Heffron Centre in 2023; the council rebuilt it during 2008 and the club returned to it in 2009 (English Wikipedia, Redfern Oval). Where it trained during the rebuild is not recorded: it grows from Redfern.

2008.name: Sydney Roosters
2008.era: The Sydney Football Stadium of 1988 was demolished in 2019; Allianz Stadium stands on its site.

2008.name: Wests Tigers
2008.era: The Tigers played their 2008 home games at Accor Stadium (4), Campbelltown and Leichhardt Oval (3 each, RLP); they grow from Concord Oval, as today.
